correctness.rationale: Using the exact pair transitions for a cycle a and one collapsing b, branch potentials L and R have componentwise ordered letter counts according to 2(j−i)<n or ≥n. The one-step Bellman inequalities F(px)≥F(p)−weight(x) have exactly one equality letter, a away from upper boundary and a/b at boundary by the gap dichotomy. Positive weights ensure strict descent to merge; any deviation strictly costs more. Cost-ratio invariance gives componentwise letter-count minimality, and unit weights partition all C(n,2) pairs into consecutive distinct distance intervals; the unique worst-pair trajectory visits all pairs. Independent reverse shortest-path computation checks all pairs for n=3..17 at four positive integer cost profiles, strict optimal letter and entire length spectrum; this finite range only corroborates the all-n argument.
residual_risks: Finite tests alone are not a universal proof.
